literal: Subjects' protection having guarded, having cherished, fault punishing, blemish is not, king's duty.
translation: Guarding and cherishing the subjects, and punishing their faults, is not a blemish but the duty of a king.
modern: குடிமக்களைக் காப்பாற்றிப் பேணி, அவர்கள் செய்யும் குற்றங்களைத் தண்டிப்பது அரசனுக்குப் பழியாகாது; அது அவனுடைய கடமையாகும்.
explanation: This couplet defines the core responsibility of a ruler regarding justice. The words 'காத்து' (guarding) and 'ஓம்பி' (cherishing) emphasize that a king must first protect and care for his subjects. When subjects commit crimes, 'கடிதல்' (punishing or removing the fault) becomes necessary. The text clarifies that such punishment is not a 'வடு' (blemish or cruelty) but rather the essential 'தொழில்' (duty) of a just king.
